No plan written: R3 has no scenario. Returned to the spec author.

The spec is approved (demo-owner, 2026-10-01T09:00Z), but R3 ("Greeting in the log", `beta.log`) has no scenario under it. My rules don't let me plan a spec with such a requirement, so I wrote nothing to `changes/add-greeting/`. R1 has scenarios R1.S1 and R1.S2, and R2 has R2.S1.

When the spec author adds an R3 scenario and the spec is re-approved, I can plan it. Two things for that scenario to settle:
- What "first line" means if `beta.log` already exists: is the file overwritten, or is the greeting appended to it?
- Whether the line in the log is exactly `hello, demo` with a newline after it.

No questions for the human.

I wrote no plan, so nothing needs filing and I printed no `DESK:` lines.

1	# add-greeting: let alpha produce a greeting that beta prints
2	
3	- size: project
4	- owner: demo-owner
5	- repos: [alpha, beta]
6	- supersedes: []
7	- approved: demo-owner 2026-10-01T09:00Z
8	
9	## Why
10	
11	Users of `beta` want a greeting on start-up, and the text belongs in `alpha`,
12	the shared library, so that other tools can use it too.
13	
14	## Scope
15	
16	In: the greeting text in `alpha`; printing it in `beta`.
17	
18	Out: translations; any change to `gamma`.
19	
20	## Requirements
21	
22	### R1 Greeting text
23	`alpha` SHALL provide the greeting `hello, demo` for a caller that asks for it.
24	
25	#### R1.S1 Default greeting
26	- GIVEN `alpha` at the branch head
27	- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with no name
28	- THEN it gets the exact text `hello, demo` (11 characters, no trailing
29	  newline)
30	
31	#### R1.S2 Name too long
32	- GIVEN a name of 65 characters
33	- WHEN a caller asks for the greeting with that name
34	- THEN it gets an error naming the 64-character limit, and no greeting
35	
36	### R2 beta prints the greeting
37	`beta` SHALL print the greeting from `alpha` as its first line of output.
38	
39	#### R2.S1 Start-up line
40	- GIVEN `beta` built against `alpha` at the branch head
41	- WHEN `beta` starts with no arguments
42	- THEN its first line of standard output is `hello, demo`, within 1 s of
43	  start (wall time)
44	
45	### R3 Greeting in the log
46	`beta` SHALL write the greeting as the first line of its log file,
47	`beta.log`, in its working directory.
48	
49	## Approaches
50	
51	1. Greeting in `alpha`, printed by `beta` (picked: one source of the text).
52	2. Greeting in `beta` only (rejected: other tools would copy the text).
53	
54	## Open calls
55	
56	1. The name limit is 64 characters, counted as Unicode code points.
